register: Rough, masculine. For polite requests use てください.

examples.gloss: Hang in there! / Go for it!

usage: A plain, blunt command. Heard from coaches, parents to children, in fiction and on signs.
Do not use it to anyone you must be polite to.
Shouted as encouragement it is warm, not rude: 頑張れ！ (Go for it!). The negative partner, 負けるな！ (Don't give up!), is encouragement too.
The negative command is ～な, built on the dictionary form: 行け (go!) and 行くな (don't go!).

compare.difference: てください is the polite request form. The imperative is only for commands.
